learningExamples: Composed teaching examples, not source quotations or recordings. Locality, generation and current frequency must be checked in the linked reference.

north.method: Only attested target words; original illustrative dialogues keep surrounding Japanese standard. Romanization is orthographic learning support, not pitch-accent guidance. No claim of universal current use.
limitations: Hokkaido entries restricted to Hakodate source context; no uniform whole-island assumption.
Tohoku additions cover Tsugaru and South Yamagata, not every assigned Tohoku subregion.
Kanto additions cover only Daigo Town within the broad Ibaraki region; other Kanto varieties were not generalized from it.
Fukui entries distinguish Reihoku, Reinan and eastern Reinan where source does.
Some words in the 2012 South Yamagata and Daigo records may be uncommon among younger speakers.
Sources attest vocabulary and definitions, not these newly composed teaching dialogues.

limitations: Examples are original learning dialogues. Surrounding grammar is standard Japanese; they are not transcripts of native local conversation.
Romanization is a readable approximation, not an accent transcription.
The Yamanashi chart and several child/clothing words are traditional; no claim that every generation still uses them.
The Niigata glossary blends prefectural varieties; all its words are assigned only to the broad niigata ID.

Primary online vocabulary evidence concentrated on Kyoto/Tango, Wakayama, Gifu/Hida, Kofu/Yamanashi, Niigata/Sado, Nagoya and Enshu. No unsupported additions were distributed to every other subregion.
Several municipal PDF opens failed; search returned indexed text with explicit target forms and meanings. These sources are labeled in the ledger.

limitations: Examples are newly composed learning dialogues. Source facts are the dialect forms, meanings and regional scopes; examples are not quoted field transcripts.
No claim of current usage frequency is made. Genkai is explicitly a historical lexicon; Shunan includes older speakers' past and heard vocabulary.
Kagawa and NINJAL prefecture-level evidence is used only on broad region IDs, without inventing narrower municipal distributions.
Ryukyuan entries are labeled by language and local variety. Okinawan Japanese is distinguished from Naha Okinawan; Hirara Miyako and Shika Ishigaki Yaeyama are not treated as one Okinawa dialect.
Romaji is a learner approximation, especially for Ryukyuan languages. No pitch-accent or exact phonetic transcription is claimed.
These additions do not repair pre-existing phrases in the pool; some existing island placeholders appear to import mainland Okinawa greetings into other language regions.
There is no new coverage for Hiroshima, Izumo, Iwami, Oki, Goto, Amakusa, Kumejima or many other southern subregions because conservative source matching took priority over spreading evidence.
